config.text: York City Walls are one of the most complex and best-preserved examples of city walls in the world, forming an essential part of York's historic townscape and civic life. The Conservation Management Plan (CMP) provides a framework for understanding their significance and guiding informed decisions on their repair, conservation and future management. This dashboard brings the CMP data into an interactive spatial platform, making heritage information accessible and supporting the ongoing stewardship of the walls.

The map brings together four key datasets from the CMP into a single spatial interface. The Introduction layer provides photographs and background information for named structures such as towers and bars. The Condition Survey layer visualises physical assessments and photographs of each wall section to support identification of areas requiring intervention. The Environmental Score and Significance Score layers display numerical scores across wall sections, allowing users to identify spatial patterns in environmental context and heritage value at a glance.

The AI agent enables users to explore CMP data through natural language queries, without manually searching through layers. Users can ask questions such as 'show me all sections in poor condition' or 'what are the policies for Bootham Bar' to retrieve targeted insights directly from the dataset. This bridges the gap between extensive paper-based records and active management needs.

The dashboard links directly to the City of York Council website and the York Planning Portal, allowing users to explore planning applications affecting the City Walls and access current policy and regulatory information. This connects the spatial analysis provided by the dashboard to the broader planning and governance context within which the walls are managed.

Developed as a strategic proof of concept for City of York Council, this platform re-engineers the York Walls Conservation Management Plan (CMP) from a static, paper-based archive into a spatially-enabled decision-making framework. By synthesizing assessments of asset condition, heritage value, and social significance into structured GIS layers, the dashboard provides an analytical environment designed to support multi-criteria stewardship and proactive policy-making for York’s fortifications.
